He was selected with the 15th pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]], was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in 2012 and was traded to Portland in 2013. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]] alongside his twin brother [[Brook Lopez]]. He played for nine NBA teams, including a three-year stint with the [[Chicago Bulls]] and two stints with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. ==Early life== Lopez was born in [[Panorama City, California]], to Heriberto Lopez, a Cuban baseball player, and Deborah Ledford, a swimmer.{{cite web|last=LaPointe|first=Joe|title=Wonderful World of Lopez Twins|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/03/26/sports/ncaabasketball/26stanford.html?pagewanted=all|work=The New York Times|access-date=April 3, 2013|date=March 26, 2008}}{{cite web|last=Gustafson|first=John|title=The nerd herd|url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?id=3608450|work=ESPN the Magazine|access-date=April 3, 2013|date=October 22, 2007}}{{cite web|last=Elling|first=Steve|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-04-29-sp-431-story.html|title=At 6-10, Alex Lopez Is Drawing a Crowd : Youth basketball: The 14-year-old's mother says many have inquired about her son, looking 'for a piece of the pie.'|work=Los Angeles Times|date=April 29, 1990|access-date=April 2, 2019}} He attended [[San Joaquin Memorial High School]] in [[Fresno, California]], where he was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in 2006. ==College career== [[File:Robin and Brook Lopez.jpg|thumb|Lopez (left) with his twin brother [[Brook Lopez|Brook]] at Stanford]] Lopez was one of just three players for the Cardinal team to start all 31 games in the 2006–07 season. He averaged 7.5 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 5.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, while averaging 24 minutes.{{Cite web |url=http://gostanford.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lopez_robin00.html |title=Robin Lopez's Stanford Player Bio |access-date=December 8, 2007 |archive-date=December 22, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071222153302/http://gostanford.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lopez_robin00.html |url-status=dead }} He led the team with 73 [[Block (basketball)|blocked shots]], breaking the Stanford record for a freshman and recording the second highest single season record in Stanford history. This mark also was the highest in the Pacific-10 conference. With his twin brother, Brook, the two blocked more shots than seven Pac-10 teams.{{Cite web |url=http://www.pac-10.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041007aab.html |title=2006-2007 Pac-10 Men's Basketball Wrap-Up |access-date=December 8, 2007 |archive-date=October 12, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012024117/http://www.pac-10.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041007aab.html |url-status=dead }} Lopez also had two [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]]s on the season. Lopez had his 100th career [[Block (basketball)|block]] in a game versus Santa Clara University on December 19, 2007. In his sophomore season, Lopez achieved All-Pac-10 Defensive Team honors while also being named an Honorable Mention to the All-Pac-10 team.[http://www.pac-10.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032608aaa.html Stanford Battles Texas Friday In NCAA Tournament Sweet 16]{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} He was second in the Pac-10 in blocks for the season. With 83 blocks in his second season, Lopez moved into second place all time for career blocks by a Stanford player. Lopez declared that he would enter the [[2008 NBA draft]] on March 31, 2008, after just two seasons at Stanford.[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3322897 Robin, Brook to enter NBA draft after two seasons at Stanford] ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2008–2012)=== Lopez was selected with the 15th overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the 2008 NBA draft. After being drafted by the Suns, Lopez said: "I was hoping I'd drop. I think I was the only person in the draft that was hoping he'd drop."{{Cite web |url=https://www.azcentral.com/members/Blog/PaulCoro/26635 |title=Suns draft chatter (with updates) |access-date=April 16, 2020 |archive-date=January 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118145535/http://www.azcentral.com/members/Blog/PaulCoro/26635 |url-status=dead }} Lopez joined a Suns team already featuring one of the all-time great centers in [[Shaquille O'Neal]], and thus was not expected to get many minutes during his rookie season. He got the first start of his career on November 7, 2008, against the [[Chicago Bulls]] in place of the injured O'Neal; he played 30 minutes, scored 14 points, grabbed 7 rebounds and had 2 blocks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=281107004|title=Suns vs. Bulls - Box Score - November 7, 2008 - ESPN}} For his rookie season, Lopez only saw an average of 10.2 minutes per game, with 3.2 points and 2 rebounds. At the end of the season, Shaq was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], making Lopez the assumed starting center.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4285489|title=Sources: Suns agree to send Shaq to Cavaliers|date=June 25, 2009}} [[File:Robin Lopez Suns.jpg|thumb|left|Lopez with the Suns in January 2011]] During the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 regular season]], Lopez averaged 8.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 1.0 block per game. During the end of the season, however, Lopez was injured, and was replaced by [[Jarron Collins]] until the Western Conference Finals against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], where the Suns eventually lost, 4 games to 2. After the 2009–10 season, Lopez went into a major decline, despite starting and playing more games. During December [[2010–11 NBA season|2010]], he was injured again, and he was temporarily replaced by [[Earl Barron]]. This eventually resulted in decreased production from Lopez, which forced the Suns to trade for [[Marcin Gortat]]. While Lopez was still starting for the Suns, his stats were quickly declining, while Gortat's stats were improving. This forced Lopez to eventually become a bench player again. Lopez would average 6.4 points and 3.2 rebounds at an average of 14.8 minutes per game. In the shortened [[2011–12 NBA season]], Lopez did not start any games for the Suns, but did play in 64 games. Because of Gortat's increased production at center, Lopez was forced to become a back-up center once again. He averaged 5.4 points with an average of 14 minutes per game there.{{Cite web |title=Robin Lopez Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3447/robin-lopez |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=ESPN |language=en}} ===New Orleans Hornets (2012–2013)=== [[File:Robin Lopez Hornets 2.jpg|thumb|right|Lopez with the Hornets in 2013]] On July 27, 2012, the [[New Orleans Hornets]] acquired Lopez and [[Hakim Warrick]] in a three-team sign-and-trade deal involving the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], which sent [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]], [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wesley Johnson]] and [[Jerome Dyson]] to the Suns.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-lopez-and-warrick-phoenix|title = Charlotte Hornets News process. ===Portland Trail Blazers (2013–2015)=== On July 10, 2013, New Orleans traded Lopez to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as a part of a three-way trade that also involved the [[Sacramento rebounds.{{cite web|title=Blazers' Robin Lopez Breaks Franchise Single-Season Offensive Rebounding Record|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2033138-pelicans-robin-lopez-breaks-franchise-single-season-offensive-rebounding-record|work=BleacherReport.com|date=April 17, 2014|access-date=May 3, 2014}} Due to his presence in the Portland community, as well as his consistent and blue-collar style of play, Lopez was a fan favorite amongst the Portland faithful. He was honored with the Maurice Lucas Award in March 2014 for his efforts in his "Read Big" literacy campaign with Portland Public Schools.{{cite web|last=Freeman|first=Joe|title=Trail Blazers' Robin Lopez honored with Maurice Lucas Award|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2014/04/trail_blazers_robin_lopez_earns_maurice_lucas_awar.html|work=OregonLive.com|date=March 19, 2014|access-date=May 3, 2014}} On December 16, 2014, Lopez was ruled out for a month after breaking his hand against San Antonio the night before.[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--robin-lopez-expected-to-miss-month-with-broken-hand-075032518.html Sources: Robin Lopez expected to miss month with broken hand] ===New York Knicks (2015–2016)=== On July 9, 2015, Lopez signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-four-free-agents-afflalo-r.-lopez-williams-oquinn|title=Knicks Acquire Four Free Agents: Afflalo, R. recorded 23 points and a career-high 20 rebounds in an 88–80 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160320/SACNYK/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins has 24 points, 20 Matthews|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-robin-lopez-and-wes-matthews|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 12, 2019|date=July 12, 2019}} ===Washington Wizards (2020–2021)=== On November 22, 2020, Lopez signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |title=Wizards sign Robin Lopez |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-robin-lopez |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 28, 2020 |date=November 22, 2020}} During his Wizards stint, his signature hookshot made him a good scoring option off the bench. On May 6, 2021, Lopez scored a season-high 24 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. Lopez had the third best field goal percentage in the whole league in the [[2020–21 NBA season]]. ===Orlando Magic (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Lopez signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Robin Lopez|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-robin-lopez-nba-free-agent-contract-20210806|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2021|date=August 6, 2021}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2022–2023)=== On July 8, 2022, Lopez signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Ricky Rubio, Robin Lopez, and Raul Neto|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-rubio-lopez-neto-signings-220708|access-date=2022-07-08|website=NBA|language=en}} ===Return to Milwaukee (2023–2024)=== On July 7, 2023, Lopez signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], reuniting him with his twin brother [[Brook Lopez|Brook]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Robin Lopez|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-robin-lopez|access-date=2023-07-07|website=NBA|language=en}} On February 8, 2024, Lopez was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] and was {{s-end}} ==Personal life== Lopez has three brothers: Chris, Alex, and twin brother [[Brook Lopez|Brook]]. Alex played college basketball for [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] and [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]],[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=3427071 All kidding aside, Lopez brothers enjoyed one fun ride] and professionally in Japan, New Zealand[https://web.archive.org/web/20150123235009/http://www.basketball.org.nz/_r/uploads/2007/02/2000-stat-leaders.pdf 2000 NBL Standings and Statistical Leaders] and Spain, while Brook also plays in the NBA for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Lopez maintains his offseason home in [[Portland, Oregon]], even though he no longer plays for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2014/11/robin_lopez_trail_blazers.html|title=Robin Lopez: Trail Blazers' missing link finds a home in Portland|date=November 26, 2014}} Lopez is an avid comic book enthusiast and also participated in theater productions at Stanford in California.[https://www.espn.com/espn/magazine/archives/news/story?page=magazine-20071022-article47 Nerd Herd – ESPN] In 2026, he publicly opposed [[Enes Kanter Freedom]] and [[Royce White]]’s attempts to join the [[WNBA]] as [[trans women]].{{Cite tweet |last=Lopez |first=Robin |user=rolopez42 |number=2086180079907024901 |date=8 August 2026 |title=Biggest issue: If you're being drafted, people are saying "we want you around for 4 years" & I can't imagine anybody wants Enes Kanter or Royce White around them for even 4 minutes.
